name: Download then run
what: Downloads a file and then runs it in the same command: {target}
why: You never get to read what was downloaded before it runs.
cost: Anything on this computer, including files and passwords, could be read or changed.
undo: there is no way to un-run it; you would have to check the damage by hand.

name: Command too long to read
what: This command is too long for Sure? to read: {target}
why: Sure? reads only the first 4000 characters, so it cannot tell you what the rest does.
cost: Anything the unread part does, including deleting files or sending data away.
undo: depends on what the command does; read it in full before you allow it.

name: Pipe download into a shell
what: Downloads code from the internet and runs it immediately: {target}
why: You never see what the downloaded code does before it runs.
cost: Anything on this computer, including files and passwords, could be read or changed.
undo: there is no way to un-run it; you would have to check the damage by hand.

name: Change database data
what: Changes or erases database data or its structure: {target}
why: Databases hold the real information your app depends on.
cost: Data can be lost for good, or the app can stop working with the old data.
undo: only if you have a backup of the database from before.

name: Damage the whole system
what: Runs a command that can break this computer or lock you out: {target}
why: These commands act on the whole system, not just your project.
cost: The computer could stop starting, lose every file on a disk, or become open to anyone.
undo: usually not; you would need a full backup or a reinstall.

name: Delete files
what: Permanently deletes files or discards your changes: {target}
why: Deleted files skip the recycle bin, and discarded changes are not saved anywhere.
cost: Your work or project files could disappear.
undo: only if the files were saved in git or a backup beforehand.

name: Push code online
what: Sends your code to a shared online copy: {target}
why: Other people or services may see or build on it straight away.
cost: A mistake becomes public, and a forced push can overwrite other people's work.
undo: possible, but it needs a second correcting push and others may already have your version.

name: Install a package
what: Adds someone else's code to your project: {target}
why: That code runs with the same access your project has, and is only as trustworthy as its author.
cost: Your project grows, and a bad or abandoned package can bring bugs or security holes.
undo: uninstall the package; this usually restores things.

name: Run a hidden script
what: Runs a script whose real actions are hidden inside it: {target}
why: The command name looks harmless but the script can do anything, including delete or send files.
cost: You are trusting the script's contents without seeing them.
undo: depends on what the script does; open the script first to find out.

name: Change Claude's own settings
what: Edits the settings that control what Claude may do without asking: {target}
why: A change here can switch off these safety prompts or widen what Claude is allowed to do.
cost: Claude could gain more freedom than you intended, without any further warning.
undo: put the old version of the file back from git or an editor's history.

name: Write inside .git or .claude
what: Writes inside a folder that holds git's records or Claude's own setup: {target}
why: These folders control how your project history and Claude itself behave; they are not normal project files.
cost: Git history, hooks or Claude's agents and commands could be damaged or tampered with.
undo: possible only if you have a copy of the folder from before.

name: Edit a secrets, login or database-change file
what: Edits a file that holds secrets, controls logins or changes the database: {target}
why: These files hold passwords and keys, decide who can sign in, or change how your data is stored.
cost: A leaked key, a lock-out, an open door for strangers, or a database change that is hard to reverse.
undo: put the old file back from git, but a leaked key must be replaced and a database change that already ran needs its own undo.

name: Edit a dependency or build file
what: Edits a file that lists the app's dependencies or how it is built: {target}
why: A small mistake here can pull in an unexpected package or stop the app from building or starting.
cost: The app may stop installing, building or starting until the change is fixed.
undo: put the old version of the file back from git or an editor's history.

name: Fetch a web page
what: Reads a web page from the internet: {target}
why: The page's content comes from outside and can contain instructions meant to mislead Claude.
cost: Little by itself, but the address you send reaches that site.
undo: nothing was changed on your computer, so there is nothing to undo.

name: Search the web
why: Your search words leave this computer and the results come from outside.
cost: Little by itself; the search terms reach a search service.
undo: nothing was changed on your computer, so there is nothing to undo.

name: Use an outside connected tool
why: Connected tools can send messages, change accounts or act in other services on your behalf.
cost: Something outside this computer may be changed or sent, such as a message or a record.
undo: often not; a sent message or changed account may need fixing by hand.

name: Start a helper agent
what: Starts a separate helper agent to do a job: {target}
why: The helper works on its own and uses the same permissions without you watching each step.
cost: It uses extra time and usage, and may change files while it runs.
undo: stop the helper and undo its changes using git or a saved copy.
